intended_object: The docstring describes the canonical isomorphism colim(F.unop) ≅ unop(lim F) for a functor F : Jᵒᵖ ⥤ Cᵒᵖ that has a limit. It holds because a limit in Cᵒᵖ is the same thing as a colimit in C.
explanation: The definition applies `isColimitCoconeUnopOfCone` to the limit cone of F. This turns the limit cone into a colimit cocone of F.unop : J ⥤ C whose cocone point is unop(lim F). `colimit.isoColimitCocone` then identifies the chosen colimit of F.unop with that cocone point. This is exactly the standard duality isomorphism. The only assumption is `HasLimit F`, which is the minimal one needed; it also yields `HasColimit F.unop`. Category and universe levels are fully general. The lemmas proved right after the definition (`ι_comp_colimitUnopIsoOpLimit_hom` and `π_comp_colimitUnopIsoOpLimit_inv`) confirm that it is compatible with the colimit injections and the limit projections. The name has a small quirk: it says "OpLimit" although the object is `unop (limit F)`. This does not change what the definition constructs. The other definitions in this file (`limitUnopIsoUnopColimit`, `colimitOpIsoOpLimit`, etc.) are different variants, not the same object.
